problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}=1?$

feedback.problem:
Complete the following parametric equations generating the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}=20$ in terms of the parameter $t,$ defined for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ where $t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sec}⁡t$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2} & =20 \\ \frac{4{y}^{2}}{20}-\frac{5{x}^{2}}{20} & =\frac{20}{20} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{5}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our case, $a=\sqrt{5}$ and $b=\sqrt{4}=2.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$
